summary.en: Pakistan’s security forces have killed five terrorists in Balochistan’s Washuk district and five more in operations in Bannu, while authorities charged Afridi and four others over the 2023 Radio Pakistan attack. The Taliban have suspended BBC broadcasts across Afghanistan and are leveraging European concerns about migrants, while Afghanistan’s road to China remains stalled. Pakistan and the EU are discussing migration and border-security cooperation, and Pakistan has imposed emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a move that could affect its ties with Afghanistan. The conflict produced 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistans sikkerhetsstyrker har drept fem terrorister i Washuk-distriktet i Balochistan og fem til i operasjoner i Bannu, mens myndighetene har siktet Afridi og fire andre for angrepet på Radio Pakistan i 2023. Taliban har suspendert BBC-sendinger i Afghanistan og utnytter europeisk bekymring for migranter, mens Afghanistans vei til Kina fortsatt er fastlåst. Pakistan og EU diskuterer migrasjons- og grense­sikkerhetssamarbeid, og Pakistan har innført unntakstilstand i Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, et tiltak som kan påvirke forholdet til Afghanistan. Konflikten førte til 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
